messages:
Mark - cust-eng: Hey team — running into a weird one on a customer's private VPC. Onprem installer + agent fails during model pull and telemetry register behind corp TLS inspection. Installs time out or show 401s.

Alice - support: Sorry — can you paste the minimal repro and any logs?

Mark - cust-eng: Yep. Repro on a clean k8s node in their VPC:
```
# installer log snippet
2024-05-05T09:12:03Z installer: fetching https://model-registry.redwood-inference.com/shards/abcd
2024-05-05T09:12:04Z http: TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2024-05-05T09:12:04Z auth: POST https://auth.redwood-inference.com/token returned 401 unauthorized
```

Mark - cust-eng: Quick curl from same node:
```
curl -v https://auth.redwood-inference.com/token -H "Authorization: Basic ..."
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate is OK
* server certificate: subject: CN=auth.redwood-inference.com
> POST /token HTTP/1.1
...
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```
So curl shows 401 but TLS looks fine. The agent logs show TLS bad certificate.

Alice - support: That discrepancy often means a transparent proxy/TLS-inspection device doing different behavior for long-lived golang clients vs curl (SNI/ALPN differences) or OCSP stapling being required by our client. Can you run openssl s_client and show the cert chain + OCSP stapling?

Mark - cust-eng: Ran these from the node (outputs trimmed):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername auth.redwood-inference.com -status
OCSP response: no response sent
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=proxy-corp.local
   i:/CN=Corp Proxy CA
```
So the cert is being replaced by the corporate proxy.

Priya - netops: That's consistent with TLS interception. Which endpoints are failing? Model registry, telemetry ingest, auth token exchange, and upstream package pulls?

Mark - cust-eng: All of the above. Also pip/apt in the installer fails intermittently: cert verify errors for files.pythonhosted.org. Model shard downloads sometimes hit CloudFront.

Jamal - security: If there's TLS inspection we need to know if the proxy is doing OCSP stapling or rewriting certs without proper chain. We require transparent proxies to allow OCSP stapling and passthrough for a handful of endpoints (auth, model registry, telemetry, package registries) because our agent validates stapled responses and checks AIA.

Alice - support: To unblock the customer while they sort proxy rules, can you request an egress allowlist (proxy bypass) for the following host groups and ports? Also include OCSP responders and CA validation hosts. Here is a concise list we typically ask customers to allow outbound to (TCP 443):
- auth.redwood-inference.com
- model-registry.redwood-inference.com
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com
- packages.redwood-inference.com (internal package CDN)
- shards.rwdcdn.net (model shard CDN, CloudFront-hosted)
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.org
- registry-1.docker.io
- s3.amazonaws.com and relevant regional S3 endpoints
- *.cloudfront.net
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org
- ocsp.apple.com (if Mac/agent envs)
- crl and ocsp endpoints for customers' corporate CA if used by the proxy

Plus these IP ranges (short-lived CDN ranges — tell us which region and we'll provide exact lists):
- (customer to request CloudFront edge ranges for their region)

Priya - netops: For our firewall change window we need exact FQDNs and whether IPs or DNS-based allow. They asked if wildcard FQDNs are ok.

Alice - support: Wildcards are ok for the CDN and telemetry if your proxy supports them. For auth and model-registry please allow exact hostnames. If the proxy cannot bypass, configure it to not intercept TLS for those FQDNs (TLS passthrough) so client cert validation and OCSP work normally.

Mark - cust-eng: Also capturing a failing agent debug trace (relevant bits):
```
2024-05-05T09:15:12Z agent: http2: server sent GOAWAY, debug: "TLS verify failed: certificate signed by unknown authority"
2024-05-05T09:15:12Z agent: retrying token exchange -> 3 attempts then fail
```

Jamal - security: If they must keep interception, we can provide an allowlist of OCSP endpoints and telemetry endpoints to be whitelisted from re-signing. But corp policy may prevent that. Request: provide the proxy vendor + firmware so security can give guidance.

Mark - cust-eng: Vendor is "BlueGate-Inspect" appliance v8.2. Customer is nervous about bypassing inspection. They asked if we can sign a trust bundle or provide a pinned CA thumbprint so they can allowlist.

Alice - support: We don't sign customer bundles. We can provide the list of required FQDNs + a note: if you must re-sign, the proxy must preserve OCSP stapling and the full cert chain, or configure a TLS passthrough for these hosts. Otherwise agent TLS checks will fail.

Lucas - csm: I'll message the customer with the recommended minimal-change path (allowlist auth/model-registry/telemetry + ocsp responders) and offer a call with NetOps.

Priya - netops: I'll open the change with the firewall team. Can you paste the exact allowlist snippet I can drop into our change ticket?

Alice - support: Copyable snippet (TCP 443):
```
# Required outbound FQDNs for Redwood agent and installer
auth.redwood-inference.com
model-registry.redwood-inference.com
telemetry.redwood-inference.com
packages.redwood-inference.com
shards.rwdcdn.net
files.pythonhosted.org
pypi.org
registry-1.docker.io
s3.amazonaws.com
*.cloudfront.net
# OCSP responders (examples — include CA-specific ones if your proxy re-signs)
ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org
ocsp.apple.com
# Note: if your proxy re-signs certs, configure it to preserve OCSP stapling and full chain OR enable TLS passthrough for the above hosts.
```

Mark - cust-eng: Thanks. I'll paste this as the customer's change request and include the BlueGate logs. Also added: they also need access to our telemetry ingestion on port 8443 for some legacy envs — we should include that if possible.

Alice - support: Added — if they open the change ticket with these FQDNs + 443/8443 and list the proxy vendor/version, we can join the call.

deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline notice — support/installer v2.6.1 rolled out to prod 2024-05-04 22:03 UTC :rocket:

Lucas - csm: Thanks everyone — I'll coordinate and confirm once the change is scheduled. :thumbsup:
